movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Linked hands forming human chains in street processions (kalejira); unrecorded or stylized in court settings.
movement_profile.footwork: Walking, marching, or stepping in time with the recurring bass or percussion pulse.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Linear street movement, winding chains, or structured court arrangements.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Low level, grounded walking and marching steps without jumps.
movement_profile.partnering: Group and collective community formation rather than closed-couple partner dancing.
movement_profile.posture: Gravitational and upright in European court styles; relaxed and upright for marching in South American street traditions.

signature_moves.description: Participants link hands to form human chains walking from street to street during community celebrations.
signature_moves.name: Street Chain

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Grave, slow, or measured in European models (around ♩ = 106 MM); animated and lively in South American street bands.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Do not treat the historical European form and the Andean popular form as identical choreographically; respect the specific regional context.

music_profile.musical_form: Variation form over a ground bass (basso ostinato), sometimes combined with rondeau elements.

reference_recordings.title: Passacaglia and Fugue in C minor, BWV 582

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Continuous variations over a repeating 4, 6, or 8-bar basso ostinato.
music_profile.sound_description: A solemn, steady foundational bass pattern anchors fluctuating upper melodies, shifting from the contemplative minor-key gravity of Baroque organ and strings to the bright, brassy, and nostalgic syncopation of Andean street bands.
music_profile.vocal_style: Instrumental origins, though later incorporated into vocal works, opera arias, and South American civic songs.

basic_steps: Walk or march in time with the underlying bass ostinato or street band rhythm.
Form human chains with other participants in street settings (as in the Basque kalejira).
Execute periodic stops during street processions to engage in secondary folk dances like the fandango.
teaching.formation: Linear street processions, human chains, or formal court configurations.
teaching.level_notes: Detailed footwork technique is not described in sources; practice focuses on rhythmic alignment with the ground bass or band accompaniment and collective movement.
teaching.rhythm: Triple metre (3/4) in European baroque forms; binary (2/4) march rhythm in South American traditions.
